justification: GATE-0 parcel-identity: stop the NSW Portal fuzzy /address search from silently binding a brief/report to the WRONG parcel (verified live: '29 Haberfield Rd' -> '29 Stanton Road'; '1 Dalhousie St' -> '15 Dalhousie Street'), which stamps every downstream figure AUTHORITATIVE for a different property. Shared verified resolver applied fail-closed at all three tracked production address resolvers.

pre_impl.existing_data: The Portal /address search is fuzzy with noOfRecords:1; three independent tracked resolvers (resolve_address, pre_da_history geocode, nsw_planning_api client) took data[0].propId with no check that the resolved address matched the request. Each response record carries an 'address' label usable for verification.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The 39-agent audit ranked this #1 'realized this run' but that run used a manual non-UI input; the brief UI uses Google autocomplete, so the nonexistent-street case can't occur there. The residual that survives autocomplete is wrong street NUMBER on the right street (Google's address set != NSW cadastre) plus all non-UI paths (CLI/API). The bulk Prospector is spatial (ST_Intersects) and not affected; geocode_addresses.py is untracked.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: New shared module services/address_identity.py is the single source of truth; the three resolvers call it and fail closed on mismatch. No change to resolution for matching addresses.
pre_impl.external_source_error: If the NSW Portal /address call errors or times out, each resolver already fails closed (retry then raise or return None). GATE-0 only inspects a successful non-empty response, so it never turns an API error into a wrong parcel and adds no new error path.
pre_impl.frontend_type: N/A - backend address resolution only; no new frontend types or boundaries. The brief UI's Google Places autocomplete sits upstream and is unchanged.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: If GATE-0 rejects a genuinely valid address whose Portal label differs (false reject), the user sees a fail-closed 'could not resolve' state rather than a brief built on the wrong parcel — visible, not silent.

functions.name: parcel_identity_match
functions.input: the requested address string and the resolved candidate address label from the Portal
functions.output: True only when street number and street name match; the requested tokens must prefix the candidate
functions.if_none: empty or sub-two-token input on either side returns False so a bare number never matches

functions.name: normalize_addr_tokens
functions.input: a free-form address string from the request or the Portal label
functions.output: ordered comparable tokens with street types expanded and state/country/postcode noise dropped
functions.if_none: an empty or whitespace-only string returns an empty token list

functions.name: resolve_address
functions.input: the requested address string for the brief/conveyancing flagship and CLI
functions.output: the resolved propId plus coordinates only when the parcel identity matches the request
functions.if_none: on a fuzzy mismatch it logs a GATE-0 line and returns None for every element (fail closed)

values: N/A - no regulatory values; the matcher compares address tokens only and hardcodes no parcel data
queries: N/A - no database queries; the gate runs on the Portal /address HTTP response already fetched by each resolver

break_it.scenario: Requested street does not exist; Portal returns a different street at the same number
break_it.what_happens: Without the gate the wrong parcel's lot area / FSR / height feed the whole brief, stamped AUTHORITATIVE
break_it.repro: resolve '29 Haberfield Rd' -> Portal returns '29 STANTON ROAD'
break_it.how: parcel_identity_match returns False (street name mismatch); resolve_address returns None and logs [GATE-0]; test covers the live label

break_it.scenario: Requested number absent on a real street; Portal returns a neighbouring number
break_it.what_happens: A real Google-valid address could still resolve to the wrong house (e.g. new subdivision, unit complex)
break_it.repro: resolve '1 Dalhousie St' -> Portal returns '15 DALHOUSIE STREET'
break_it.how: street number must match exactly (req[0] == cand[0]); returns False; tested

break_it.scenario: Formatting differences between Google input and Portal label
break_it.what_happens: A correct address could be falsely rejected (abbreviations, unit prefix, missing postcode)
break_it.repro: '29 Dalhousie St' / '5/29 Dalhousie Street' vs '29 DALHOUSIE STREET HABERFIELD 2045'
break_it.how: normalize_addr_tokens expands street types, drops state/country/postcode, reduces unit 5/29 to 29; both accept-cases tested

break_it.scenario: A future edit removes the gate from one of the three resolvers
break_it.what_happens: The wrong-parcel bug regresses silently on that path
break_it.repro: delete the parcel_identity_match call from any production resolver
break_it.how: test_gate_applied_at_all_production_resolvers asserts the call is present in all three files

break_it.scenario: NSW Portal /address API errors or times out during resolution
break_it.what_happens: A transient API failure could be misread as a resolved parcel
break_it.repro: Portal returns a non-200 or times out mid-resolve
break_it.how: GATE-0 runs only on a successful non-empty response; on error each resolver already retries then raises or returns None (fail closed), so GATE-0 adds no new error path

post_merge.manual_verify: Run a CLI/API brief for a non-existent street number on a real street and confirm it fails closed (no brief for the wrong parcel) with a [GATE-0] log line. This is GATE-0 of the capacity-engine remediation (~/.claude/plans/ce-capacity-engine-audit-2026-06.md); the legality gates (permissibility/dwelling-count, SEPP-on-heritage) are the larger next steps and remain unexposed until done.
